 Early voting opens in Alaska’s midterm elections
 Alaska Public Media | 
 By
 Eric Stone 
 Published October 19, 2026 at 4:00 AM AKDT
 Twitter 
 LinkedIn 
 Email 
 Bluesky 
 Matt Faubion 
 / 
 Alaska Public Media Voters cast their ballots in the 2022 primary election in Anchorage on Aug. 16, 2022. 
 Early voting for the midterm elections is officially underway across most of Alaska. Polls opened Monday morning for the 15-day period leading up to Election Day on Nov. 3.
 Alaskans are voting this year on races for U.S. Senate, U.S. House, governor and the state Legislature, plus two ballot measures.
 In Anchorage, voters can cast early ballots at the Midtown Mall, Anchorage City Hall and Eagle River Town Center from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. weekdays, with shorter hours on the weekends.
 Early voting is also available at the Menard Sports Center in Wasilla, the Matanuska-Susitna Borough Building in Palmer, the State Office Building in Juneau and Division of Elections offices in Fairbanks, Kenai, Nome and Juneau.
 Voters in other communities can vote early using what’s known as “absentee-in-person” voting, where voters can fill out ballots in person that are then mailed to election offices. Locations for absentee-in-person voting include city halls, tribal government offices, schools and community centers.
 Voting hours vary by location.
 A list of early voting sites is online at elections.alaska.gov/avo .
 Voters can also request a mail ballot, for any reason, before Oct. 24 .
 To learn more about where the candidates stand on the issues, read our election coverage, watch debates and check out a voter guide put together by Alaska Public Media, the Anchorage Daily News, the Alaska Beacon and KTOO. You
 Polls will be open on Election Day, Nov. 3, from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m.
 In many high-profile races, results aren’t expected until the Division of Elections tabulates voters’ ranked choices on Nov. 18.
